title: Complexity of Deciding PSD Polynomial Sum-of-Squares

problemStatement.plain: What is the computational complexity of deciding if a given PSD polynomial is a sum of squares.

knowledge.progressSummary: Session (researcher-1, 2026-06-24): proved the UNIVARIATE case of Hilbert's 17th (Hilbert 1888) with a fully elementary, 0-axiom Lean proof — every non-negative p : ℝ[X] is a sum of two squares of polynomials (new child entry hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-04, Proofs/Hilbert17UnivariatePSDSOS.lean) — and wired it into the parent, discharging the axiom univariate_psd_is_sos_aux (parent axiomCount 3 → 2). Route: strong induction on degree; FTA gives a complex root; a real root of a PSD poly has even multiplicity (one-sided-limit sign argument) so (X-C r)² factors out; a non-real root contributes a positive real quadratic (X-C z.re)²+(C z.im)² that divides p, recombined via Brahmagupta–Fibonacci. This is the positive counterpart to the Motzkin/Robinson counterexamples (the polynomial conclusion holds only in one variable). The 2 remaining parent axioms (quadratic_psd_is_sos_aux, pfister_bound_aux) are the genuinely deep independent ones.
builtItems: Hilbert17UnivariatePSDSOS.univariate_psd_is_sos (verified, 0-axiom): every non-negative univariate real polynomial is a sum of two squares, Proofs/Hilbert17UnivariatePSDSOS.lean

insights: The univariate case has an elementary induction-on-degree proof needing only the FTA plus continuity: the sole analytic input is that a real root of a non-negative polynomial has multiplicity ≥ 2 (if it were simple, p=(x-r)g changes sign across r — one-sided limits force g(r)≥0 and g(r)≤0). Real roots come out as (X-C r)², conjugate pairs as a positive quadratic, and the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity keeps everything a sum of two squares. No real-closed-field or Gram-matrix machinery — and unlike n≥2, the conclusion is genuine polynomials, not rational functions.

Robinson non-SOS has an elementary zero-set proof: R's ten real projective zeros (1,±1,0),(1,0,±1),(0,1,±1),(1,±1,±1) impose ten INDEPENDENT conditions on the ten-dimensional space of ternary cubic forms (the 10×10 evaluation matrix has determinant 128 ≠ 0), so any cubic form in an SOS decomposition of R must be zero. The coefficient-cascade method (which works for Motzkin) genuinely fails for Robinson because its pure powers x⁶,y⁶,z⁶ have nonzero coefficients — but the zero-set method sidesteps that entirely.
Motzkin non-negativity is a polynomial AM–GM inequality that nlinarith closes from square hints (x²y²−1)², (x²y−y)², (xy²−x)²; no transcendental cube-root argument is needed at the eval level.

Robinson's polynomial equals Schur's expression a(a−b)(a−c)+… under a=x², b=y², c=z²≥0, so its non-negativity is exactly Schur's inequality — nlinarith finds the constrained certificate from a·(a−b)² ≥ 0 terms.

Three of the parent hilbert-17 axioms were redundant restatements, not independent assumptions: artin_hilbert17 and cassels_bound_bivariate are specializations of pfister_bound_aux (take m=2^n; and 2^2=4 defeq gives the n=2 case directly), and artin_univariate is the algebraMap image of the stronger polynomial result univariate_psd_is_sos_aux. All three now derived as theorems — axiom count 7 → 4.

Eliminating a redundant axiom is honest axiom reduction: when axiom B is provable from axiom A already in the file, B was never adding assumptive content, so converting B to `theorem ... := <derivation>` genuinely shrinks the independent-assumption set.
nextSteps: Attempt quadratic_psd_is_sos_aux (PSD quadratic form = SOS of linear forms) via the Gram matrix: poly↔symmetric A, A PSD ⟹ A = BᵀB (Mathlib Matrix.PosSemidef / Cholesky-spectral), Q = ‖Bx‖². The poly↔matrix bridge is the main work.
